subject: Vireo: Log retainability artefact delivery plan
messages:
From: Jane Park <jane.park@vireotherapeutics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Vireo: log retention and proof-of-delete details

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking this on. Our external SOC 2 auditor has asked for customer-specific evidence that demonstrates Redwood's deletion path and log retention controls for tenant-scoped debug traces. Specifically they requested: 1) excerpt from your retention policy showing default TTL for ephemeral inference logs, 2) a walk-through or runbook for 'proof-of-delete' (how you validate an erasure request finished), and 3) a redacted example of deletion logs or API audit entries showing an executed erase for a tenant (timestamps and flow, redacted PII).

We also have CAIQ and SIG mapping questions around whether debug traces are considered "ephemeral" vs. "audit" data in your environment and whether you support customer-requested retention exceptions (we may need a 90-day forensics hold for a subset of tenants). Could you confirm whether Redwood can provide a signed attestation for a temporary retention exception, and what controls you put around privileged access to retained traces?

We need the package by end of next week (2026-12-29) for the audit. Happy to hop on a quick call if useful.

Thanks,
Jane Park
Head of Security Assurance
Vireo Therapeutics

---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@vireotherapeutics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vireo: log retention and proof-of-delete details

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely assemble the package. Quick answers up front:

- Default: ephemeral inference/debug traces are retained 30 days by default; audit trails tied to account changes are retained longer per our SOC 2 policy.
- Proof-of-delete: we have an automated deletion workflow plus an attestation artifact (hash + deletion job id) we can export per request.
- Exceptions: we can support customer-scoped temporary retention holds (e.g., 90 days) with an internal approval workflow and limited access session recording.

I want to make sure what you need in the deliverable: full CAIQ/SIG mappings + CAIQ response, the redacted deletion log example, and a short runbook (PDF) showing the erase workflow and verification steps. We'll attach the artifacts and provide a short summary for the auditor.

Can you confirm whether the auditor needs signed (wet-signed) letters, or a Redwood-signed PDF attestation will suffice? Also confirm the tenant id(s) we should use for the redacted log sample (we can use synthetic IDs if needed).

I'll coordinate a package and loop in Marissa and Rishi to pull the CAIQ responses and deletion logs.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

- Marissa: CAIQ + SIG mapping, and a short narrative that explains where debug traces land in our data classification (ephemeral vs audit). Please include any CAIQ controls that reference log retention or deletion process.
- Rishi: Export a redacted sample deletion log (CSV) + the signed PDF runbook for proof-of-delete. Also add the internal approval email chain that demonstrates exception gating.

Attachments to include in final outbound package: CAIQ response (zipped), proof_of_delete_runbook.pdf, sample_deletion_log_redacted.csv. Put the files in the compliance Drive folder and share links to Jane.

Notes: keep tenant identifiers synthetic (vireo-TEST-001) to avoid exposing PII. For the attestation, we'll use a Redwood-signed PDF (legal okay with this unless Jane says otherwise).

Thanks — Ben
